40: People assume I must be rich, sitting beside so much money all day. I assure them the two facts are unrelated.
41: My hands have touched more money than most people ever see. My own wallet remains deeply unimpressed.
42: I slide the money across the counter and then it is gone. It is always going somewhere without me.
43: Every day I count to enormous numbers. Then I go home and count my own coins in about four seconds.
44: I know exactly how heavy a thousand coins is. Nobody has ever once asked me to demonstrate this.
45: People hand me their savings and I smile and give it right back. I am the least greedy person alive.
46: I have counted this drawer eleven times today. The number keeps agreeing with itself. Reassuring.
47: There is a pen chained to my counter. It has outlasted three of my coworkers. We are very close now, that pen and I.
48: I say the same eight sentences to every customer. By closing time they no longer sound like words.
49: I stamp things. I stamp so many things. If it holds still long enough, I will stamp it too.
50: I have a little sign that reads next window please. Sliding it into place is the most powerful thing I do all day.
51: I keep the money in neat, even piles. My desk at home is chaos. I ran out of neatness at work.
52: A person came to deposit a jar of coins. We counted them together for an hour. Best morning all week.
53: I hand out crisp new notes all day. They are lovely. I get to admire each one for about two seconds.
54: My whole job is being extremely careful with numbers that belong to strangers. I have never lost one.
55: I smile at everyone through a small window. By evening my face forgets how to do anything else.
56: I have moved the same fifty in and out of this drawer so often we are practically old friends now.
57: People trust me with their money the moment we meet. Nobody trusts me to pick a restaurant. Curious.
58: I recount whenever the total is off by one coin. Usually the coin is under my own shoe. Usually.
59: All day the money flows past me like a river. I am the person standing in it, staying completely dry.
60: I run this hotel. I have seen every kind of guest. Nothing surprises me. I practice that face daily.
61: A guest asked for a room with a better echo. I said of course. I have learned to just say of course.
62: In this job you see everything. Twice. Then a third thing arrives and quietly ruins your afternoon.
63: Someone requested extra pillows. Then fewer pillows. Then, thoughtfully, the exact same pillows back.
64: I keep a calm face no matter what walks through that door. Inside, I am often mildly astonished.
65: A guest complained the ocean was too loud. I nodded and wrote it down. There is nothing I can do about the ocean.
66: A guest asked me which direction the wind usually comes from. I gave my most confident guess. He wrote it down.
67: I have a smile for every situation. I have run out of situations before I have run out of smile.
68: A guest wanted the fourth floor moved to the second. I explained the building. He seemed let down.
69: My desk has a small bell. Guests ring it while looking directly at me. I still arrive, promptly, from zero distance.
70: Every guest believes their request is the strangest I have ever heard. They are all, somehow, correct.
71: I have kept this desk calm through weddings, storms, and one very determined goat. Do not ask me.
72: I say welcome about three hundred times a day. My face means it roughly two hundred of those times.
73: A guest asked if the elevator could go faster. I said I would speak to it. We had a good talk.
74: I have seen luggage that could not possibly fit through the door. It always fits. I stopped asking why.
75: The trick to this job is looking perfectly calm while, underneath the desk, both of my feet are quietly panicking.
76: A guest wanted a room far from the elevator, far from the stairs, and near the exit. I drew him a small diagram.
77: I keep the whole hotel running smoothly. The guests think it runs itself. I let them keep thinking so.
78: A guest told me their room was haunted. I offered a different room. It was, they reported, also haunted.
79: A guest asked me to name the best room. They are all the best room. I have delivered that line, calmly, for years.
